definicaoChebi.texto: A one-carbon compound that is methane in which the hydrogens have been replaced by three chlorine and one fluorine atom.
A glucopyranose having D-configuration.
A fructopyranose having D-configuration.
A galactopyranose having D-configuration.
D-Mannose in its six-membered ring form.
A D-ribose and the D-enantiomer of ribopyranose.
A deoxypentose that is D-ribofuranose in which the hydroxy group at position C-2 is replaced by hydrogen.
D-Xylose in its pyranose form.
A glycosyl glycoside formed by glucose and fructose units joined by an acetal oxygen bridge from hemiacetal of glucose to the hemiketal of the fructose.
The β-anomer of lactose.
A glycosylglucose consisting of two D-glucopyranose units connected by an α-(1→4)-linkage.
A glycosylglucose consisting of two glucose units linked via a β(1→4) bond.
The D-enantiomer of glucitol (also known as D-sorbitol).
The D-enantiomer of mannitol.
A pentitol (five-carbon sugar alcohol) having meso-configuration, being derived from xylose by reduction of the carbonyl group.
An amino acid zwitterion arising from transfer of a proton from the carboxy to the amino group of glycine.
Zwitterionic form of L-alanine arising from transfer of a proton from the carboxy to the amino group; major species at pH 7.3.
An L-α-amino acid zwitterion obtained by transfer of a proton from the carboxy to the amino group of L-valine; major species at pH 7.3.
Zwitterionic form of L-leucine.
An L-α-amino acid zwitterion obtained by transfer of a proton from the carboxy to the amino group of L-isoleucine; major species at pH 7.3.
The zwitterion formed from L-proline by proton transfer from the carboxy group to the ring nitrogen. It is the predominant species at physiological pH.
An amino acid zwitterion arising from transfer of a proton from the carboxy to the amino group of L-phenylalanine; major species at pH 7.3.
An L-α-amino acid zwitterion obtained by transfer of a proton from the carboxy to the amino group of L-tryptophan; major species at pH 7.3.
Zwitterionic form of L-methionine having a anionic carboxy group and a cationic amino group; major species at pH 7.3.
The L-enantiomer of serine.
Zwitterionic form of L-threonine arising from transfer of a proton from the carboxy to the amino group; major species at pH 7.3.
An optically active form of tyrosine having L-configuration.
An optically active form of asparagine having L-configuration.
An optically active form of glutamine having L-configuration.
The L-enantiomer of aspartic acid.
An optically active form of glutamic acid having L-configuration.
An L-α-amino acid; the L-isomer of lysine.
An L-α-amino acid that is the L-isomer of arginine.
Zwitterionic form of L-histidine having an anionic carboxy group and a protonated α-amino group.
The zwitterion formed from taurine by transfer of a proton from the sulfonyl to the amino group. It is the major species existing at physiological pH.
A glycine derivative having methyl and amidino groups attached to the nitrogen.
The parent compound of the 6-aminopurines, composed of a purine having an amino group at C-6.
A 2-aminopurine carrying a 6-oxo substituent.
An aminopyrimidine that is pyrimidin-2-one having the amino group located at position 4.
A pyrimidine nucleobase that is uracil in which the hydrogen at position 5 is replaced by a methyl group.

A common and naturally occurring pyrimidine nucleobase in which the pyrimidine ring is substituted with two oxo groups at positions 2 and 4. Found in RNA, it base pairs with adenine and replaces thymine during DNA transcription.
A ribonucleoside composed of a molecule of adenine attached to a ribofuranose moiety via a β‒N^(9)-glycosidic bond.
An adenosine 5'-phosphate in which the 5'-phosphate is a triphosphate group. It is involved in the transportation of chemical energy during metabolic pathways.
A cholestanoid consisting of cholestane having a double bond at the 5,6-position as well as a 3β-hydroxy group.
An androstanoid having 17β-hydroxy and 3-oxo groups, together with unsaturation at C-4‒C-5..
The 17β-isomer of estradiol.

A C₂₁-steroid hormone in which a pregnane skeleton carries oxo substituents at positions 3 and 20 and is unsaturated at C(4)-C(5). As a hormone, it is involved in the female menstrual cycle, pregnancy and embryogenesis of humans and other species.

A 17α-hydroxy-C₂₁-steroid that is pregn-4-ene substituted by oxo groups at positions 3 and 20 and hydroxy groups at positions 11, 17 and 21. Cortisol is a corticosteroid hormone or glucocorticoid produced by zona fasciculata of the adrenal cortex, which is a part of the adrenal gland. It is usually referred to as the "stress hormone" as it is involved in response to stress and anxiety, controlled by corticotropin-releasing hormone (CRH). It increases blood pressure and blood sugar, and reduces immune responses.
The R-enantiomer of adrenaline. It is a hormone secreted by the adrenal glands resulting in the 'fight-or-flight' response.
The R-enantiomer of noradrenaline.
Catechol in which the hydrogen at position 4 is substituted by a 2-aminoethyl group.
A primary amino compound that is the 5-hydroxy derivative of tryptamine.

A member of the class of acetamides that is acetamide in which one of the hydrogens attached to the nitrogen atom is replaced by a 2-(5-methoxy-1H-indol-3-yl)ethyl group. It is a hormone secreted by the pineal gland in humans.
A member of the class of imidazoles that is 1H-imidazole substituted at position C-4 by a 2-aminoethyl group.
Zwitterionic form of γ-aminobutyric acid having an anionic carboxy group and a protonated amino group.
